definitions.type: family of finite-dimensional real metric vector spaces indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: For m∈ℕ, V_m=EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m), with norm (sum over i∈Fin m of |x_i|²)^(1/2). This is Euclidean ℝ^m. V_0 is the singleton empty-coordinate vector space. Each V_m and ℝ carry their Borel measurable structures. A product of two metric spaces in this proof has distance max of the factor distances.
I=[0,1]={t∈ℝ:0≤t≤1}; the metric is the usual real distance.

definitions.type: Hausdorff-measure family indexed by real exponent on metric spaces with Borel structure
definitions.definition: For a real exponent a and a subset T of a metric space X with Borel measurable structure, μH[a](T)=sup over r∈ℝ≥0∞, r>0, of inf over U:ℕ→Set X with T⊆⋃i U_i and ediam(U_i)≤r of ∑'i sup_{h:U_i.Nonempty}(ediam U_i)^a. Here ediam is the supremum of distances of pairs in the set, valued in ℝ≥0∞, and ediam ∅=0. The inner supremum is zero for an empty set. For a>0 this is exactly the unnormalized diameter-power countable-cover measure: empty members cost zero and no multiplicative normalization constant occurs. μH[a] denotes MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure a.

binders.type: metric space with its Borel measurable structure

definitions.type: Hausdorff dimension of subsets of metric spaces, valued in ℝ≥0∞
definitions.definition: For a subset T of a metric space X, dimH T=sup{a∈ℝ≥0 : μH[a](T)=∞}, using the canonical embedding ℝ≥0→ℝ≥0∞ and the Borel measurable structure. This is the library Hausdorff dimension; dimH∅=0. In particular all dimension comparisons and additions in this graph take place in ℝ≥0∞ unless an explicit real conversion is written.
F=E×I={p∈V_n×ℝ:p.1∈E and p.2∈I}, with the max product metric from D001.

A_m(x,t)=appendCoord m (x,t) is the vector whose coordinate i.castSucc is x(i) for i∈Fin m and whose coordinate Fin.last m is t. Precisely appendCoord m p=(EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.snoc ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ) p.1) p.2). This supplies only the coordinate map, with no continuity, isometry or dimension-invariance assertion.

euclideanProduct n E=A_n''F, the image under appendCoord n of E×I. Its elements have first n coordinates x∈E and last coordinate t∈[0,1]. It has the Euclidean metric of V_(n+1). Image notation f''T means {f(x):x∈T}.

inputs.statement: For the given nonempty E⊆Euclidean ℝ^n, dimH(E×[0,1])=dimH E+1 in the max product metric.

For n∈ℕ define A_n(x,t)∈V_(n+1) by first n coordinates x and last coordinate t (appendCoord). For every set S⊆V_n×ℝ, dimH(A_n''S)=dimH S, where S has the max product metric and its image has the Euclidean metric.

hypotheses: The map is exactly appendCoord m, with the stated source and target metrics.

output.statement: For every integer n≥0 and every nonempty compact E⊆Euclidean ℝ^n, the coordinate copy of E×[0,1] in Euclidean ℝ^(n+1) has Hausdorff dimension dimH E+1. The coordinate copy consists of (x₁,…,x_n,t) with x∈E and 0≤t≤1; for n=0 it is the unit interval in Euclidean ℝ. Hausdorff measures use the unnormalized diameter-power convention and dimH∅=0.

argument.text: Instantiate E005 at the given n and S=F⊆V_n×ℝ. Its map is the exact append-coordinate map A_n of D007, with max metric on its source and Euclidean metric on its target. It therefore gives dimH(A_n''F)=dimH F. By D008, A_n''F=euclideanProduct n E, so dimH(euclideanProduct n E)=dimH F. This source conclusion is the required change of metric and coordinate identification.

Substitute N006, dimH F=dimH E+1, into F001. Thus dimH(euclideanProduct n E)=dimH E+1 with the required Euclidean metric and coordinate description. The given n and E were arbitrary, so this proves P under the original hypotheses. When n=0, D001 makes V_0 the singleton empty-coordinate vector space, and D007 sends (x,t) to the vector whose sole coordinate is t; hence the same statements cover this boundary case. All measures are those of D003, with the unnormalized diameter-power convention at the positive exponents used in the proof and the dimension convention of D004.

applications.bindings: Set the source ambient index m=n and source set S=F. Use precisely A_n=appendCoord n as defined in D007.
hypothesis_checks: n is a natural number and F⊆V_n×ℝ by the parameters, D001 and D005.

D007 defines exactly appendCoord n. D001 and D005 give the max metric on the source; D001 and D008 give the Euclidean metric on the image. Thus E005 delivers invariance for the actual two metrics needed here.
